stem: A pharmacy took its last complete controlled-substance inventory 25 months ago. What is the issue?

choices.text: Use the out-of-state prescription rule when its schedule, age, and verification conditions have not been checked.
Process another refill because an authorization written by the prescriber overrides schedule limits.
Treat the request as an insufficient-stock partial fill and use the 72-hour remainder rule.
Handle the drug or transaction as ordinary Massachusetts Schedule VI activity.
The federal biennial inventory interval has been exceeded.

explanation.core_reasoning: After the initial inventory, each registrant must take a new controlled-substance inventory at least every two years. The pharmacy must use the exact trigger and deadline rather than borrowing a nearby controlled-substance rule.

choice_analysis.A: That choice belongs, if at all, to Out-of-state Schedule III through VI prescriptions; its trigger does not match this scenario.
choice_analysis.B: That choice belongs, if at all, to Federal Schedule III and IV refill limits; its trigger does not match this scenario.
choice_analysis.C: That choice belongs, if at all, to Schedule II partial fill caused by pharmacy inability; its trigger does not match this scenario.
choice_analysis.D: That choice belongs, if at all, to Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription-drug status; its trigger does not match this scenario.
choice_analysis.E: This applies Biennial controlled-substance inventory: After the initial inventory, each registrant must take a new controlled-substance inventory at least every two years.

related_facts: After the initial inventory, each registrant must take a new controlled-substance inventory at least every two years.
explanation.mpje_trap: Applying schedule iii-iv refills to facts controlled by biennial inventory.

reasoning_steps: Identify the trigger for Biennial controlled-substance inventory
Separate the controlling pathway from a nearby rule with a different schedule, deadline, or setting
Apply the exception and documentation conditions before selecting the final pharmacy action
